goal.summary: MPI-372 is DONE, USER-VERIFIED and COMMITTED as ebd5a82f; the card is in the done column. The headline finding is that the canvas/preview swap the brief called the design blocker is a VRAM optimisation, not a display requirement - so the fix was to not swap at all. completed: MPI-372 SHIPPED + USER-VERIFIED + COMMITTED (ebd5a82f). Mask tools keep the canvas AND show the PromptBox; `prompt` remains a rail tool and still swaps to the light preview surface.

THE KEY INSIGHT, do not re-litigate it: swapToPreview() destroys MpiCanvas to release GPU texture backing (~100MB per 4K image) and mounts MpiMaskedImagePreview, two in a CSS stack. The preview is a STRICT SUBSET of the canvas. A mask tool already keeps the canvas mounted and already draws the mask, so no swap is needed. The coupling was never `prompt => preview`, it was `no canvas tool => cheap surface`.

Round 2 defect A: the op strip yanked the rail to prompt mode. MpiPromptBox._refreshOpStrip routes clicks through Events.emit('workspace:set-operation'), and the Block's handler force-called setMode('prompt'), which ran swapToPreview() and destroyed the canvas mid-mask. DELETED, not gated - the whole mechanism is vestigial (see key_decisions).

Round 2 defect B: mask state was published ONLY on tool exit - evaluateMask() had exactly two callers, the two mask organisms' destroy(). Painting emitted nothing, so the op strip never unlocked mask-only ops. Added the missing publisher through existing plumbing: InputController._endMaskStroke() -> MpiCanvas onMaskStrokeEnd -> MpiCanvasViewer._publishMaskState() -> the existing evaluateMask() -> the existing mask-ready handler. Emits only on a FLIP, so it is one signal per transition, not one per stroke. Space-cancel routes through the same helper.

Round 2 defect C: loadEntry's sameEntry guard skipped the persist but still ran _showEntry + _restoreLayers, restoring a TEMP that predated the live strokes - so re-clicking the entry a mask lived on wiped it. Now returns early when the same entry is already on a live canvas WITH content; the mount case has an empty canvas and still falls through to the load path it needs.

Round 2 defect D: _reloadViewerWithEntry called exitMode() BEFORE loadEntry, throwing away the mode loadEntry captures and restores. The rail showed an armed mask tool over a canvas in mode 'none' - no brush on a fresh result until you re-clicked the card. Fixed by dropping the pre-emptive exit and re-arming from the rail via a new _syncViewerToolMode() that entry-selected now shares.
Round 2 defect E: the op strip hovers above the prompt bar (position:absolute, bottom:100%) over the bottom 35px of the history list. .mpi-group-history-block__right gained padding-bottom: 2.5rem.
Both MpiCanvas mounts (initial + swapToCanvas remount) now share ONE _canvasProps object so a callback can never be wired on only one of them.

key_decisions: THE SURFACE SWAP IS A VRAM OPTIMISATION, NOT A DISPLAY REQUIREMENT. swapToPreview() destroys MpiCanvas to free GPU texture backing; MpiMaskedImagePreview is a strict subset of the canvas. Mask tools therefore do not swap at all. Do not reintroduce a swap for any new mask tool - Shapes and Text inherit the correct behaviour free via _isMaskTool().

THE RADIAL-ERA OP FORCE IS DELETED, DO NOT BRING IT BACK. `workspace:set-operation` now has exactly ONE emitter, MpiPromptBox._refreshOpStrip, and the strip lives INSIDE the PromptBox - so by the time the event fires the box is on screen by construction and the workspace never needs to change tools to serve it. The Block still VALIDATES the op against live context (mask present, history mode); the strip is a second view of that state, not a source of truth for it. MpiGalleryBlock's handler never forced a mode. The frame-grab setMode('prompt') is behind `if (!isVideo) return;` and can never collide with an image-only mask tool.

MASK STATE IS NOW PUBLISHED AS IT CHANGES, not only on tool exit. Any new mask tool gets this free - it comes from the canvas' own stroke-end signal, not from the tool. If a new tool creates a mask by some other means (a shape commit, a text detection), it must emit mask-ready itself or call viewer.el.evaluateMask(), or the op strip will not unlock.

THE RAIL IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for which canvas tool is armed. Both viewer-reload paths (entry-selected and _reloadViewerWithEntry) go through _syncViewerToolMode(). They had already drifted once - keep them sharing it.
BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: a generation finishing while CROP is active now leaves crop armed too (it used to silently disarm). Consistent with the rail; flagged to the user, who did not object.

Carried from the previous session and still true: the mask strip is ONE component on every mask tool (brush+eraser pair optional); MpiMaskDetectRow is shared by Points, Detect and later Text; ONE toolKey ('mask') for the whole family so settings survive a tool swap; AUTO PICKS UNION LAST, with TWO twins - MaskManager._recomposite() and MpiCanvasViewer._buildCompositeFromTemp() - that must change together; the colour split is DISPLAY-ONLY and getURL()/getMaskDataURL() must keep flattening the single unioned maskCanvas.
Rail tool modes are maskDetect / maskPoints; the viewer knows only canvas modes 'crop' and 'mask'. _viewerModeFor() bridges them and any new mask tool must be added to _isMaskTool().

context.verification_recipe: The live-app harness that proved MPI-372 is reusable and cheap. Node script requiring playwright by ABSOLUTE path (c:/AI/Mpi/Cubric-Vision/node_modules/playwright) so it runs from the scratchpad; goto with waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' NOT 'networkidle' (the app holds SSE streams open so networkidle never settles); a fresh page has no project, so import /js/services/projectService.js and call listProjects() + openProject() before router.navigate(PAGE_GROUP_HISTORY, { groupId }). Rail buttons carry the tool NAME in [data-info] ('Detect', 'Points', 'Crop', 'Prompt'), NOT the mode key. ALWAYS pair a pass with a NEGATIVE CONTROL: back the files up, `git show HEAD:<path>` over them, re-run, restore, and diff to prove the restore. A green run with no negative control proves nothing about what the harness measures.
